items.q: Pseudopalisading necrosis with microvascular proliferation in an adult cerebral tumour defines what grade and type?
items.exp: Glioblastoma (grade 4) requires necrosis and microvascular proliferation in an astrocytic tumour, showing ring enhancement and butterfly spread with dismal prognosis despite therapy.
r: Incorrect. Pilocytic tumours are grade 1 childhood cystic lesions.
Correct. Those features define grade 4 glioblastoma.
Incorrect. Meningiomas are dural extra axial tumours graded differently.
Incorrect. Metastases show primary cancer histology at grey white junctions.
items.kp: Necrosis plus new vessels in glioma equals highest grade.

items.q: A child with vermis tumour, Homer Wright rosettes and spinal drop metastases has what?
items.exp: Medulloblastoma is an embryonal small blue cell tumour of cerebellar vermis in children seeding CSF to spine, needing craniospinal staging and therapy. Homer Wright rosettes support neuroblastic differentiation.
r: Incorrect. Pilocytic tumours rarely seed CSF and form cyst nodules.
Correct. Vermis plus rosettes plus seeding means medulloblastoma.
Incorrect. Ependymoma forms perivascular pseudorosettes in ventricles.
Incorrect. Choroid tumours cause hydrocephalus by overproduction location.
items.kp: Child vermis tumour that seeds the spine: medulloblastoma.

items.q: Slow growing dural based mass with whorls, psammoma bodies and dural tail is what?
items.exp: Meningiomas arise from arachnoid cells forming dural masses with whorled meningothelial cells and calcified psammoma bodies, mostly benign and surgically curable.
r: Incorrect. Schwannomas arise from nerve sheaths with Antoni areas.
Correct. Dural whorled tumour is meningioma.
Incorrect. Glioblastoma infiltrates brain parenchyma necrotically.
Incorrect. Neurocytoma is intraventricular neuronal tumour of young adults.
items.kp: Dural tail plus psammoma whorls equals meningioma.

items.q: Cerebellopontine angle tumour with Antoni A and B areas causing unilateral hearing loss is what?
items.exp: Vestibular schwannomas grow on cranial nerve eight at the cerebellopontine angle causing sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus, with biphasic Antoni A (cellular, Verocay bodies) and B (loose) histology. Bilateral tumours define NF2.
r: Incorrect. Angle meningiomas lack Antoni pattern histology.
Correct. Antoni areas on nerve eight mean schwannoma.
Incorrect. Ependymomas are ventricular, not angle nerve tumours.
Incorrect. Epidermoid cysts are keratin filled congenital lesions.
items.kp: Angle plus hearing loss plus Antoni means schwannoma; bilateral means NF2.

items.q: Bitemporal hemianopia with galactorrhoea and raised prolactin indicates which pituitary tumour?
items.exp: Prolactinoma secretes prolactin causing galactorrhoea and hypogonadism, and when macroadenoma expands upward compresses the chiasm cutting temporal visual fields. Dopamine agonists shrink most.
r: Incorrect. Non functioning tumours lack prolactin excess signs.
Correct. Prolactin excess plus chiasm compression means prolactinoma.
Incorrect. Craniopharyngioma is suprasellar cystic, not prolactin secreting.
Incorrect. Apoplexy is haemorrhage into an existing tumour emergency.
items.kp: Milk plus temporal field loss: prolactinoma at the chiasm.

items.q: Calcified suprasellar cyst with wet keratin in a child with growth failure suggests what?
items.exp: Craniopharyngioma (adamantinomatous in children) forms calcified cysts with cholesterol rich fluid and wet keratin above the sella, damaging vision, growth and thirst regulation.
r: Incorrect. Prolactinoma is intrasellar prolactin secreting.
Correct. Calcified suprasellar cyst in a child means craniopharyngioma.
Incorrect. Rathke cysts are benign midline without wet keratin tumours.
Incorrect. Germinomas favour pineal and suprasellar with diabetes insipidus but differ histologically.
items.kp: Child suprasellar calcified cyst equals craniopharyngioma.

items.q: Perivascular pseudorosettes in a fourth ventricle tumour of a child indicate what?
items.exp: Ependymomas arise from ventricular lining forming perivascular pseudorosettes and true rosettes, obstructing CSF in the fourth ventricle of children and spinal cord (myxopapillary) in adults.
r: Incorrect. Medulloblastoma forms Homer Wright rosettes in vermis.
Correct. Pseudorosettes mean ependymoma.
Incorrect. Pilocytic shows Rosenthal fibres and cyst nodule.
Incorrect. Meningioma is dural in adults predominantly.

items.q: Multiple ring enhancing lesions at grey white junctions in a smoker most likely are what?
items.exp: Metastases outnumber primary tumours in adults, lodge at grey white junctions with disproportionate oedema and multiplicity, lung being commonest source. Solitary butterfly necrosis favours glioblastoma instead.
r: Incorrect. Multiple primaries are rare.
Correct. Multiple junction lesions mean metastases first.
Incorrect. Abscesses need infection context and diffusion features.
Incorrect. Demyelination gives open ring patterns with different course.
items.kp: Many lesions at junctions in adults: hunt the primary cancer.

items.q: Cystic cerebellar tumour with mural nodule and Rosenthal fibres in a child, often cured by excision, is what?
o: Hemangioblastoma of von Hippel Lindau only
items.exp: Pilocytic astrocytoma (grade 1) forms cyst with enhancing mural nodule in child cerebellum with Rosenthal fibres and eosinophilic granular bodies, carrying excellent surgical prognosis.
r: Incorrect. Medulloblastoma is solid vermis embryonal and seeds CSF.
Correct. Cyst plus nodule plus Rosenthal means pilocytic.
Incorrect. Ependymoma is ventricular with pseudorosettes.
Incorrect. Hemangioblastoma favours adults and VHL screening.
items.kp: Best prognosis child brain tumour: pilocytic cyst and nodule.

items.q: Thunderclap headache with sudden visual loss and ophthalmoplegia in a pituitary tumour patient is what emergency?
items.exp: Pituitary apoplexy is haemorrhage or infarction of an adenoma causing headache, visual failure, ophthalmoplegia and hypopituitarism needing immediate steroids and neurosurgical evaluation.
r: Incorrect. SAH lacks the pituitary hormonal collapse pattern.
Correct. Bleeding adenoma causes apoplexy emergency.
Incorrect. Meningitis adds fever and neck stiffness without this gland picture.
Incorrect. Sinus thrombosis causes proptosis and chemosis patterns.
items.kp: Pituitary mass plus thunderclap plus blindness: apoplexy. Give steroids fast.
